```{python}
#| include: false
import sys
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path.cwd().resolve().parent
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT))
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "scripts"))
import report_values  # noqa: E402

v = report_values.compute()
r = v["raw"]


def md_table(header, rows):
    lines = ["| " + " | ".join(header) + " |", "|" + "|".join([":--"] * len(header)) + "|"]
    lines += ["| " + " | ".join(str(c) for c in row) + " |" for row in rows]
    return "\n".join(lines)
```

This page holds the statistical detail behind the [organizer summary](en.qmd). Every number is read from the simulation outputs when the site is rendered. The model, its assumptions and the sources are on the [Methods](methods.qmd), [Assumptions](assumptions.qmd) and [Literature](literature.qmd) pages.

Two kinds of interval appear. An interval "of the median" is a 95% bootstrap interval for the typical night. A "range across nights" covers 5% to 95% of the simulated nights and shows how different one plausible night is from another.

## What was observed and what matches it

The 2026 observations come from the attendees who ran this study. At 15:30 buying was relatively quick, although it still took a while. Between 18:00 and 20:00 (God Module and Das Ich) the beer exchange line alone took more than 40 minutes for a person who already held tickets, both the ticket line and the exchange lines were long, and a lot of people gave up. After 20:00 they stopped trying to buy, so every wait after that hour is a prediction of the model. The hall was near its fullest around 22:00. One window sold tickets for every drink, two lines exchanged beer and one exchanged cocktails and shots, and people bought several beers per visit for friends.

Waits are reported as the median time until service, estimated with the Kaplan-Meier method. A person who gave up waited at least until leaving the line, and counting that time as a completed wait would understate lines in which many people give up.

The unknown inputs (how many people drink and how fast, patience, group size, people serving beer, time per ticket sale and per beer) were sampled with a sequential approximate Bayesian computation sampler. Of `{python} v["sims"]` simulated nights in `{python} v["stages"]` stages, `{python} v["matching"]` pass every test in the last stage (effective sample size `{python} v["ess"]`). A weighted resample of `{python} v["post_n"]` nights is used for everything below. In those nights `{python} v["pour_2026"]` people serve beer, the ticket window takes a median of `{python} v["window_s"]` s per buyer and the first beer of a visit `{python} v["serve_s"]` s.

In the matching nights, between 18:00 and 20:00, the ticket line holds `{python} v["ticket_line"]` people and the beer exchange lines `{python} v["exchange_line"]`. A person who joins an exchange line waits `{python} v["base_exchange_wait"]` min (range across nights `{python} v["base_exchange_wait_lo"]` to `{python} v["base_exchange_wait_hi"]`), the ticket window takes `{python} v["base_ticket_wait"]` min, and a buyer without tickets needs `{python} v["base_buyer_wait"]` min for the whole purchase (`{python} v["base_buyer_wait_lo"]` to `{python} v["base_buyer_wait_hi"]`). The predicted wait in the exchange line at 21:30 to 22:30 is `{python} v["base_night_wait"]` min (`{python} v["base_night_wait_lo"]` to `{python} v["base_night_wait_hi"]`). The hall holds `{python} v["occ_med"]` people at its fullest (range across nights `{python} v["occ_lo"]` to `{python} v["occ_hi"]`), and the bar sells `{python} v["base_beers"]` beers (`{python} v["base_beers_lo"]` to `{python} v["base_beers_hi"]`). The width of that last range is the reason the number of beers sold in 2026 is the first record requested from the organizers.

![](assets/figures/01_calibration_posterior.png){fig-alt="Range tried and matching values for each unknown input"}

The two line tests require at least `{python} r["min_line"]` people in each line. A stricter reading of 30 people keeps about half of the nights. The plan performs as follows in the two groups.

```{python}
#| output: asis
rows = [("at least 30 in each line" if x.strict else "20 to 30 in one of the lines", int(x.nights),
         f"{x.wait_2026:.0f}", f"{x.wait_plan:.1f}", f"{x.extra_beers:+,.0f}")
        for x in v["threshold_check"].itertuples()]
print(md_table(["Nights", "Count", "Wait of 1 in 10 buyers in 2026 (min)", "With the plan (min)",
                "Extra beers with the plan"], rows))
```

| Outcome, 18:00 to 20:00 | Three inputs with the largest effect, in order |
|:--|:--|
| Wait in the exchange line | `{python} v["drv_wait"]` |
| People in the ticket line | `{python} v["drv_ticket"]` |
| People in the exchange lines | `{python} v["drv_exchange"]` |

## Effect of each setup

Every setup reruns the same `{python} v["nights"]` nights with the same people and the same random seed, so each difference is that night's counterfactual. The plan is payment at the serving station with `{python} v["plan_taps"]` stations and `{python} v["plan_sellers"]` roaming sellers on the floor from `{python} v["sellers_hours"]`. The wait of 1 in 10 buyers is taken over everyone who joins a line between `{python} v["svc_window"]`, the hours in which lines formed in 2026.

```{python}
#| output: asis
eff = v["effects"]
order = ["more_cashiers", "presale_bundles", "sellers_6", "satellite", "pay_at_tap", "cashless",
         "peak_shift", "full_setup", "plan"]
rows = []
for scn in order:
    w = eff[(eff.scenario == scn) & eff.outcome.str.startswith("Wait of 1 in 10")].iloc[0]
    b = eff[(eff.scenario == scn) & eff.outcome.str.startswith("Beers")].iloc[0]
    rows.append((w.label,
                 f"{w.med:+.1f} ({w.med_lo:+.1f} to {w.med_hi:+.1f})",
                 f"{b.med:+,.0f} ({b.med_lo:+,.0f} to {b.med_hi:+,.0f})",
                 f"{int(w.improved_n)} of {int(w.n)} (at least {100 * w.improved_lo:.0f}%)",
                 "< 0.001" if w.p_wilcoxon < 0.001 else f"{w.p_wilcoxon:.3f}"))
print(md_table(["Setup", "Wait of 1 in 10 buyers, min (interval of the median)",
                "Beers sold (interval of the median)",
                "Nights with a shorter wait (exact 95% lower bound)", "Wilcoxon p"], rows))
```

![](assets/figures/05_counterfactual_effects.png){fig-alt="Effect of each setup on the wait, beers sold and abandoned attempts"}

With the plan the wait of 1 in 10 buyers falls by `{python} v["d_wait"]` min (interval of the median `{python} v["d_wait_lo"]` to `{python} v["d_wait_hi"]`) to `{python} v["plan_p90"]` min, and the bar sells `{python} v["d_beers"]` more beers (`{python} v["d_beers_lo"]` to `{python} v["d_beers_hi"]`; range across nights `{python} v["d_beers_p05"]` to `{python} v["d_beers_p95"]`). At an assumed MXN `{python} v["price"]` per beer that is MXN `{python} v["d_mxn"]` in sales (`{python} v["d_mxn_lo"]` to `{python} v["d_mxn_hi"]`). Costs of staff and card fees are not in this figure.

![](assets/figures/04_wait_by_time.png){fig-alt="Typical time in line by time of joining for each setup against 2026"}

## The plan against the alternatives

Differences on the same night, second setup minus first, with the 95% interval of the median.

| Comparison | Wait of 1 in 10 buyers | Beers sold | Staff |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| Pay at the station with the 2026 head count, then the plan | `{python} v["plan_vs_tap_wait"]` | `{python} v["plan_vs_tap_beers"]` | `{python} v["plan_vs_tap_staff"]` |
| The plan, then wristbands + satellite bar + 4 sellers | `{python} v["full_vs_plan_wait"]` | `{python} v["full_vs_plan_beers"]` | `{python} v["full_vs_plan_staff"]` |
| Card or cash at the station, then cashless wristbands | `{python} v["cashless_vs_tap_wait"]` | `{python} v["cashless_vs_tap_beers"]` | `{python} v["cashless_vs_tap_staff"]` |

Roaming sellers sell `{python} v["seller_share"]` of the beers under the plan (range across nights `{python} v["seller_share_lo"]` to `{python} v["seller_share_hi"]`). A seller carries `{python} v["seller_load"]` beers per trip and refills at an end of the bar in `{python} v["seller_refill"]` min. There were no sellers in 2026, so these rules are assumptions, and the crew without sellers is the fallback.

Payment at the station with the same head count as 2026 leaves a wait of `{python} v["tap_p90"]` min for 1 in 10 buyers (up to `{python} v["tap_p90_hi"]` min in the worst 5% of nights).

## Staffing reliability

A night meets the target when 9 of 10 buyers who join a line between `{python} v["svc_window"]` wait at most `{python} v["tgt_wait"]` min and at most `{python} v["tgt_ab"]` of purchase attempts are abandoned. A crew is recommended when it meets the target in at least `{python} v["reliability"]` of the nights, and among those the one with the fewest staff hours is chosen. For `{python} v["tickets"]` tickets that crew meets the target in `{python} v["plan_met"]` nights (exact 95% lower bound `{python} v["plan_share_lo"]`).

![](assets/figures/12_staffing_reliability.png){fig-alt="Share of nights in which each crew meets the waiting target, by ticket level"}

```{python}
#| output: asis
rows = []
for row in v["staffing_rows"]:
    if row.get("taps") is None:
        rows.append((f"{row['tickets']:,}", "no crew in the grid reaches the reliability", "", "", "", ""))
    else:
        rows.append((f"{row['tickets']:,}", row["taps"], row["sellers"], f"{row['met']} of {row['nights']}",
                     f"{row['wait_median']:.1f} / {row['wait_bad']:.1f}", f"{row['staff_hours']:.0f}"))
print(md_table(["Tickets", "Stations", "Sellers", "Nights that meet the target",
                "Wait of 1 in 10 buyers, median night / bad night (min)", "Staff hours"], rows))
```

The bad night is the 90th percentile across nights.

## Capacity

The free floor (audience area without vendor strips and tables) is `{python} v["floor_m2"]` m². At `{python} v["tickets"]` tickets the people standing on it at the fullest moment amount to `{python} v["density_at_plan"]` per m². NFPA 101 caps assembly areas of up to 930 m² at `{python} v["lim"]` people/m², and the free floor reaches that value near `{python} v["cap_tickets"]` tickets. For larger areas the cap is `{python} v["lim_large"]` people/m², which the free floor reaches near `{python} v["cap_tickets_large"]` tickets. The free floor is below 930 m² and the whole audience area, with vendor strips and tables, is above it. The hall size comes from a satellite image without a scale bar, with an uncertainty near `{python} v["hall_side"]` per side. A hall that much smaller or larger reaches the first value at `{python} v["cap_tickets_lo"]` or `{python} v["cap_tickets_hi"]` tickets. That range comes from rescaling the floor area, without new simulations. The licensed capacity is the legal limit.

![](assets/figures/13_capacity.png){fig-alt="People per m² of free floor at the fullest moment against tickets sold"}

## Time-series models

A regression of beers sold per 5 minutes on people inside and a changeover indicator, with AR(1) errors, was fitted on each night from 18:00 to 02:00. In 2026 each extra 100 people inside added `{python} v["ar_b"]` beers per 5 minutes and with the plan `{python} v["ar_p"]`. A bar whose sales do not follow the crowd is at its limit. The event study shows the lines building after each set ends.

![](assets/figures/09_time_series_models.png){fig-alt="Event study of people in lines around the end of a set and AR(1) regression coefficients"}

## Drinking

With faster service the share of attendees who drink 6 beers or more rises from `{python} v["heavy_base"]` to `{python} v["heavy_plan"]` (range across nights `{python} v["heavy_plan_lo"]` to `{python} v["heavy_plan_hi"]`). Abbott and Abbott (2000) recommend purchase limits and refusing service to intoxicated patrons, and alcohol was the most common arrest reason in the stadium survey of Ammon and Fried (1999).

## Sensitivity to the calibration ranges

```{python}
#| include: false
import pandas as pd

sens_path =ROOT / "output" / "tables" / "sensitivity_ranges.csv"
stf_path = ROOT / "output" / "tables" / "sensitivity_staffing.csv"
has_sens = sens_path.exists() and stf_path.exists()
```

A first calibration used narrower ranges: patience 25 to 110 min, drinking pace before 18:00 from 0.3 to 1.0 of the evening pace, and 1 to 5 tickets per visit to the ticket window. Its matching nights gathered near the upper limit of patience and the lower limit of the afternoon pace, so part of the result came from where those limits were set. The current calibration widens the three ranges (25 to 180 min, 0.1 to 1.0, 1 to 8) and adds the test on purchase attempts given up between 18:00 and 20:00. The table compares the two runs. The values are the median night and, in brackets, the range across nights (5% to 95%). The two runs simulate different nights, so the p-value is from a Mann-Whitney U test.

```{python}
#| output: asis
if has_sens:
    sens = pd.read_csv(sens_path)

    def cell(x, k):
        if "share of purchase" in x["quantity"]:
            fmt = "{:.0%}"
        elif abs(x[f"{k}_med"]) >= 100:
            fmt = "{:,.0f}"
        else:
            fmt = "{:.2f}" if abs(x[f"{k}_med"]) < 1 else "{:.1f}"
        return f"{fmt.format(x[f'{k}_med'])} ({fmt.format(x[f'{k}_lo'])} to {fmt.format(x[f'{k}_hi'])})"

    def p_text(p):
        return "" if pd.isna(p) else ("< 0.001" if p < 0.001 else f"{p:.3f}")

    rows = [(x.quantity, cell(x._asdict(), "reference"), cell(x._asdict(), "current"),
             p_text(x.p_mann_whitney)) for x in sens.itertuples()]
    print(md_table(["Quantity", "Narrow ranges", "Wide ranges", "p"], rows))
```

```{python}
#| output: asis
if has_sens:
    stf = pd.read_csv(stf_path)
    rows = [(f"{x.n_total:,}", x.n_pour, x.sellers,
             f"{x.reference_met} of {x.reference_nights}" + (" (recommended)" if x.reference_recommended else ""),
             f"{x.current_met} of {x.current_nights}" + (" (recommended)" if x.current_recommended else ""),
             p_text(x.p_fisher)) for x in stf.itertuples()]
    print(md_table(["Tickets", "Stations", "Sellers", "Nights that meet the target, narrow ranges",
                    "Same, wide ranges", "p (Fisher)"], rows))
```

The second table lists every crew recommended in either run with the nights in which it meets the service target under each calibration. Fisher's exact test compares the two shares.

```{python}
#| output: asis
if has_sens:
    need = r["reliability"]
    lvl = stf[stf["n_total"] == r["tickets"]]
    both = lvl[(lvl["reference_met"] >= need * lvl["reference_nights"])
               & (lvl["current_met"] >= need * lvl["current_nights"])]
    if len(both):
        names = " and ".join(f"{x.n_pour} stations with {x.sellers} sellers" for x in both.itertuples())
        print(f"For {r['tickets']:,} tickets, {names} meet the target in at least "
              f"{need:.0%} of the nights under both calibrations.")
    else:
        print(f"For {r['tickets']:,} tickets, no crew in the table meets the target in at least "
              f"{need:.0%} of the nights under both calibrations.")
```

## Limits of the study

- The calibration rests on the account of the attendees who ran this study. Sales, entries and service times were not measured.
- People walk in straight lines and pass through each other, so the model cannot compare line layouts, barriers or walkways. Those recommendations come from the literature.
- Cocktails and shots, food, restrooms and evacuation are outside the model.
- There were no roaming sellers in 2026, so the seller rules (how far a seller is seen, time per sale, beers per trip, refill time) are assumed. Under the plan the sellers sell `{python} v["seller_share"]` of the beer, so the recommended crews depend on those rules.
- The hall size is an estimate from a satellite image.
- Sales in MXN use an assumed price and exclude costs.

The commands below rebuild every output from the configuration files. The steps and their inputs are described on the [Methods](methods.qmd) page.

```bash
uv sync --group site && rv sync && rv activate
./scripts/run_all.sh
```
